column3: **Request a corrected policy-scope/conflict-surface design and reconcile the duplicate gate for the HOME-search proposal?** Concrete proposal: [role artifact contract](planned/m-fleet-role-artifact-contract.md), frozen SHA df93fee6c072bbdc19850126963049a50ff7df7cd3db13cc573a08e4fd859998. One mandatory revision completed through a quota fallback; final quorum BLOCKED (OpenAI reject, Google pass; both author vendors excluded) and independent MiniMax FAIL/N/A. Remaining premise claims compliance with every standing rule from recipe-only evidence; strict planned-doc duplicate scores1.00/0.95/0.90 remain unresolved. **A (recommended):** request corrected scope-limited policy evidence, inventory/precedence/conflict surface and duplicate-gate reconciliation; a later explicit design approval is still required before planning. **B:** leave current behavior unchanged; ticket stays open. Default if unanswered: B immediately; no planning/execution/merge. No P2 command cap or routing/quota/billing change authorized.

**`skill:idle-record-barred-on-degraded-no-pick-fire` (world, 11-09): narrow Gate 5's idle-record "degraded fire" bar? The design was blocked twice by quorum.** Measured at iteration 97: no product mission has ever promoted an idle fingerprint; World 363–370 never recorded, because every fire fell back somewhere. The bar was a fleet-controller choice (`33190af48`, iteration 91), not a ruling. [Design](planned/m-idle-record-degraded-bar.md): keep the failed-read and unfinished-gate bars, drop the lane-fallback bar, and require each candidate's only unblock event to be a dev-side OPEN ledger flip. Round 2 found two real defects: the proof block ignores the ledger parser's exit status (reproduced by the judge), and no recorded World fire would qualify, because World 370's gates are external predicates, a weekly sweep and a branch-only D-WORLD-113. **A:** one more bounded revision applying every round-2 fix (sol's exit-status capture verbatim; a retro-analysis of the last 10 World and Stapledon no-pick fires, where "do not land" is an acceptable result; a falsifiable observation criterion; a cited no-pick gate list), then one re-quorum, then plan, build and judge. **B (recommended):** no change. On the evidence, the narrowed rule would not have engaged for the mission that filed the ticket. World can make it engage on its own side by recording attended steps as rulings on dev-side ledger rows. The ticket stays open until you rule. Default if unanswered: B. Not HD-2a policy class (judge agrees); this asks because the design failed its gate, not because of policy. **Iteration 127 (measured; recommendation unchanged):** 6 slots lost now, first World 370, latest World 416 and 417. Since `ff08818ae` World's fingerprint `head=` stays on the product commit `0e9e8d35`, so record commits no longer wake it. Every World fire since 2026-11-17 is degraded (codex lane), which bars the record. The bar is not the only blocker, though: a recorded 416 would not have idled 417, because 416 acked its own inbox message (inbox 1 → 0). Of the 8 World fires from 11-19 01:39Z to 11-20 05:39Z, at most 3 could have skipped even if every one had recorded. B's premise was measured on World 370; World 410–417 name the dev-side OPEN rows D-WORLD-119/120 as their gate, the shape the narrowed rule targets. Whether every World candidate's only unblock event is a ledger flip is UNMEASURED. [Judge](fleet-mission-evidence/iteration127/idle-judge.md). **Iteration 128 (measured; recommendation unchanged):** 7 slots lost, latest World 418. World 418's idle snapshot is byte-identical to 417's (`0355e1e2…`, 4 h apart, inside the 24 h expiry), so a recorded 417 would have let 418 exit at the idle pre-check: the first World slot the degraded-fire bar measurably cost on its own. Whether 417 met Gate 5's other record conditions is UNMEASURED. Of the 9 World fires from 11-19 02:39 to 11-20 10:39 local, this is the one that would have skipped; 416 → 417 still differed (inbox). World 418's gate list names attended and fleet-waiting rows besides D-WORLD-119/120, so the narrowed rule's "only a ledger flip unblocks" test stays unmeasured. The judge notes A is a reasonable choice on the forward case (head now stable). [Judge](fleet-mission-evidence/iteration128/idle-judge.md). **Iteration 129 (measured; recommendation unchanged):** 9 slots lost, latest World 419 and 420. World 420's idle snapshot is byte-identical to 419's (`dae8092b…`, `head=301131e`, 4 h apart), a second identical pair after 417 → 418; 419's own record commits did not move `head` (the `ff08818ae` exclusion holds). 418 → 419 differed: PR #619 landed product commit `301131e7`. Over World's 12 fires 11-19 02:39 → 11-20 18:39 local, exactly 2 (418, 420) would have skipped had every eligible no-pick fire recorded; the rest changed head or inbox, or fell past the 24 h expiry. Whether 417 and 419 met Gate 5's other record conditions is UNMEASURED. The pair does not touch the round-2 defects, and World 419's gate list names rows (150, 151, 263) unblocked by attended work, so the "only a ledger flip unblocks" test is still not shown to hold. World measured the codex ration gap still open at 18:38 (used 22.0% vs allowed 21.6%), so degraded fires and the bar continue. [Judge](fleet-mission-evidence/iteration129/idle-judge.md). **Iteration 130 (recommendation unchanged):** 10 slots, latest World 421. Its idle snapshot (`c3c1a8b1…`, `head=a51307d`) differs from 420's because World PR #629 landed product code between them, so it adds no identical pair (still 2 of the last 13 World fires). [Judge](fleet-mission-evidence/iteration130/idle-judge.md). **Iteration 131 (measured; recommendation unchanged):** World 422 (undegraded) recorded its idle fingerprint over the snapshot it shares with 421 (`c3c1a8b1…`), and World 423 then exited at the idle pre-check, "idle, nothing spent": the first product-mission idle skip on record, so this row's opening premise is out of date. The degraded-fire bar now costs a slot only while World's codex lane is over ration, which further weakens A. 421 → 422 is a third identical pair (with 417 → 418 and 419 → 420); the ticket's slot count is unchanged at 10. [Judge](fleet-mission-evidence/iteration131/idle-judge.md).

**May the fleet resolve the seven open tickets whose attended fixes merged on 2026-11-16?** Measured at iteration 123: the merges are #2347 → `41c628b94` (`quorum:gpt6-1-sol-openai-api-credits-exhausted`, row 21), #2349 → `005641f82` (`pi:openrouter:uncapped-max-tokens-402`, row 50), #2348 → `509146d24` (`executor:codex-credential-collision-drops-automatic-planner-handoffs`, `executor:codex-credential-lease-collision-fails-concurrent-dispatch`, row 54; `coordinator:job-retry-success-dropped-after-failed-completion`, row 55) and #2343 → `ad2148b23` (`executor:3h-timeout-from-queue-and-unsliced-sprints`, `executor:timeout-loses-work-and-may-never-start`, row 56). All seven are still open after three days, so clause 2 keeps counting them. Iteration 115 recorded them as the attended session's claim, and the fleet has touched none. Rows 18 and 24 (config rollouts with no PR) are not included. **A**: the fleet resolves each ticket, one per fire as bookkeeping, after re-checking at HEAD that the merged fix covers the ticket's own repro, and cites the merge SHA. **B**: leave them to the attended session. **Recommendation: A**, because each has a merged, reviewed fix and the reply tells the filing mission. **Default if unanswered: B** (no change). **Iteration 127 correction: an eighth ticket belongs here.** `quorum:claude-p-ration-usage-429` (D-FLEET-28 A) merged attended as #2344 → `0222baeb9`, an ancestor of origin/dev, and is still open. It had no queue row; it is now row 68. Under A it is resolved the same way.
